title: The vote calculator tallies by a rule the runtime never runs: one outcome rule
body:
## Summary
The Ranks page's 'Try a vote' calculator re-implements ballot tallying with a different rule than the runtime runs. It reports head-count and weight winners side by side with a 0.05 tie band, while the runtime decides by weight, breaks weight ties on more voters, hands true ties to the host, and drops votes below the poll's minimum rank. Make the outcome rule one thing: a TS `pollOutcome` that mirrors runtime `outcome`, pinned to it by a single fixture file both test suites read.

## Description
Leans on audience-steering-economies / sublinear-vote-weight ('The tally': weight decides, a weight tie goes to more distinct voters, a full tie goes to a pre-announced rule; give the host both numbers and announce when head-count and weight winners differ). The runtime already does this (runtime.rs:338-361); the console does not, so the one surface that teaches the operator how a weighted ballot resolves teaches a rule that differs on every equal-weight ballot (common with weights 1.0/2.0). The move: (1) crates/shadowrunr-segments/tests/data/poll_outcomes.json lists tallies -> expected verdict; a #[cfg(test)] case in runtime.rs feeds them to `outcome`; (2) model.ts replaces the verdict half of `tally` with `pollOutcome(tallies)` returning Winner/Tie/NoVotes plus a `diverges` flag (head-count leader differs from winner); model.test.ts imports the same JSON (resolveJsonModule is on in apps/console/tsconfig.json); (3) the calculator gains a poll minimum-rank select (default thrall), greys rows below it, counts ignored votes, and prints the runtime's verdict followed by the divergence sentence. The calculator stays local and sends nothing.

## Flow
- Write fixture + failing Rust and TS fixture tests
- Implement pollOutcome; keep heads/weight/max bars
- Wire calculator: min-rank select, excluded rows, verdict + divergence line
- Update layer2 DOM tests to the new verdicts

## Expected impact
The operator reads the same decision the show will make on air; a future change to the runtime rule fails the console's fixture test instead of drifting silently.

## Evaluation
Claim: the calculator's verdict equals the runtime outcome for every fixture ballot and honours poll min rank.
Before: 1 of 6 acceptance cases pass (only the START_VOTES weight winner agrees)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: none

Routing note (critic, run challenge-2026-10-21): Restated stage-kit-scene-engine A; the residue is S: the console vote calculator should call stage-kit leaders() instead of its own tie rule.
evidence: model.ts:179 `const weightWord = Math.abs(weight.a - weight.b) < 0.05 ? "The weight ties." : ...`; runtime.rs:348 `if t.weight > b.weight + 1e-9 || (level && t.voters > b.voters) { top = vec![t]; } else if level && t.voters == b.voters { top.push(t); }`; runtime.rs:1204 `if rank < p.min_rank { events.push(ignored("poll_min_rank")); continue; }`; ranks.toml weights 1.0/1.4/1.7/2.0/2.2/2.4; layer2.test.tsx:131 expects 'Head-count: A wins. Weight: B wins.'
instrument: the card's own acceptance cases, trimmed to its S core

title: Personas activity is green with a wrong secret: prove delivery in one command
body:
## Summary
Setting up Personas activity today is: configure, start the daemon, run a sim, then read daemon stderr hoping for a 'refused' line. A wrong or rotated secret leaves PF-09 green ('trigger answers'), `personas status` says 'on (secret set)', and every event is silently refused - `rejected` is counted in no figure the operator or console sees. Make the verdict one command and make PF-09 tell the truth.

## Description
(1) `shadowrunr personas status --send-test` signs and POSTs one `{source, kind:'test', ts_ms, project_id?}` body (no show data) to the configured trigger through the same deliver path and classifies the answer: delivered / refused (401/403 = signature or secret mismatch) / trigger_not_found (404) / http_<n> / unreachable, with exit codes 0/1/1/1/3 matching status.rs's existing ladder. Plain `status` never sends; its activity line says 'unverified'. (2) The forwarder records `last_rejected` (status code) beside `rejected`; PF-09 turns Amber with 'N refused (HTTP 401: secret mismatch?)' when rejected > 0, and shows refused next to delivered/dropped. The test kind is never in KNOWN_EVENTS, so configuration cannot route show events to it. Leans on the failure-not-empty-success law as mcp-tools/tool-schema-design states it ('failed calls reading as successes downstream'), applied to the outbound integration; settings stay secret-by-name.

## Flow
- `personas status --send-test` -> settings + secret env -> one signed test POST -> verdict line + exit code
- daemon forwarder refusal -> stats.rejected, stats.last_rejected -> PF-09 Amber 'refused' (the console preflight board shows it with no console change)

## Expected impact
Secret/trigger misconfiguration is found in one command instead of after a show; PF-09 stops reporting green while every event is refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: the operator can verify the signed path and PF-09 reflects refusals
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no --send-test; PF-09 Green on refusal)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first against the existing Fake webhook in activity_tests.rs (personas_verify port)
Result: better
Gate: contract

Routing note (critic, run challenge-2026-10-21): Excluded: widens the Personas webhook payload (a contract another repository consumes) and fires the persona's trigger.
evidence: forwarder.rs:478-480 `pub fn dropped(&self) -> u64 { self.failed + self.dropped_full + self.dropped_down + self.lagged }`; activity.rs:353 `format!("; {} delivered, {} dropped", s.delivered, s.dropped())`; activity.rs:371-373 `Some(200) => rep(HealthState::Green, ... "trigger answers"`; status.rs:358 `let secret = if std::env::var(a.secret_env.trim()).is_ok_and(|v| !v.trim().is_empty()) { "set" }`; docs/guide/personas.md:65 'the **PF-09** line is green when the trigger answers'.

title: A chosen character diff is only shown: let the owner apply and revert it
body:
## Summary
Reconcile spends an LLM call, a mechanical verifier and a hunk-matching check to produce a character_change diff the owner can trust, then shows it read-only. Choosing it only turns it into a spoken order in the Lord's dispatch; the bible on disk never changes, so the next tournament measures the old character under the same instrument hash. Add `option.apply` / `option.revert`: one click applies the exact diff the owner saw, re-verified against the current files, all-or-nothing, with a recorded pre-image to undo.

## Description
The verifier already proves applicability (verify.rs:501-561); the missing half is the write. `apply.rs` extends the parsed patch with new-side lines, re-runs check_diff against characters_root at apply time (the staleness window between report and click), binds the request to `diff_sha` of the stored diff so the approved content cannot be swapped, writes each file atomically, and records `AppliedChange {option_id, file, before_sha, after_sha, pre_image_path, applied_ms, reverted_ms?}` on the StoredReport. Revert restores the pre-image only while the file still hashes to after_sha. constitution.md and non-bible/tone paths stay refused by the same check_diff. Techniques: hitl-approval/gate-state-machines (the owner's click is the only open transition, consumed once; content swapped before execution is refused) and hitl-approval/oracle-before-gate (the owner reviews the exact bytes that are applied); undo per undo-history/checkpoint-restore. Gate: direction (the console gains an owner-initiated write into the character package; no model output is ever applied without that click).

## Flow
- owner opens Plan options and reads the verified diff
- clicks Apply to package -> option.apply {report_id, option_id, diff_sha}
- daemon re-verifies, writes bible.md / tones/*.md atomically, records the pre-image
- card flips to Applied + Revert; the next tournament picks up the new instrument hash on its own
- Revert -> option.revert restores the pre-image if nobody edited since

## Expected impact
A proposed character improvement goes from 'read diff, open an editor, hand-copy hunks, hope it matches' to one click with undo, and the change reaches the next measured tournament instead of only the dispatch text.

## Evaluation
Claim: an owner-approved, verified diff is applied exactly, refused when stale or swapped, and reversible.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no apply/revert method exists)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen

Routing note (critic, run challenge-2026-10-21): Excluded from challenge mode: first runtime write path of model-composed, chat-derived text into the owner's tracked bible.md/tones, which feed the trusted prompt. Needs the owner by name.
evidence: verify.rs:501-502 '/// Validate a `character_change` diff. With `character_dir`, also check that every hunk's old side matches the current file, so the owner is never shown a diff that cannot apply.'; grep 'fs::write|write_json_atomic|write_atomic' | grep -i 'bible|tone|charact' over crates -> only verify.rs test lines and sim/src/instrument.rs tests; lib.rs:558-560 choose ends `stored.plans.push(plan.clone()); self.save(&stored)?; write_json_atomic(&self.cfg.data_dir.join("next_plan.json"), &plan)?;`; synth.rs:401 'It must convey every chosen option and every active directive'; PlanPage.tsx:74 `{o.diff !== undefined && o.diff.length > 0 && <DiffView diff={o.diff} />}` followed by the checkbox 'Choose for the next stream'; daemon rpc.rs:265-268 plan.choose is the only plan write method.

title: The on-air command card is a hand copy of the segment table, and it has drifted
body:
## Summary
The standing card the broadcast shows between explainers tells viewers which chat commands they can use. It is a hand copy of the Rust segment table, and it has already drifted. In SEG-02A it leaves out `!propose`, which the table allows, and it shows `!propose <scheme>` where the parser documents `<text>`. Derive the card from one committed artifact that a Rust test generates and gates for drift.

## Description
Today OnAir.tsx hard-codes five CommandRow constants and a per-segment switch (OnAir.tsx:43-58). The real vocabulary lives in `COMMAND_SPECS` (command.rs:21) and in each segment's `commands = [...]` (data/segments/*.toml). The daemon derives it for the console (catalog.rs:490), but the stage has no RPC and replays have no daemon, so it copied the data. This is the registry's `segment-as-state-table` failure mode 'the frozen view' (and 'prose duplicating the table'): an operator or viewer surface that projects the table and stops following it. The move follows `codegen` / drift-gating plus commit-vs-derive-policy. A new integration test in shadowrunr-segments renders `{segment -> [{name,args,what,rank_gated}]}` from `table::tables()` and `COMMAND_SPECS` in table order, with a `_generated` provenance key. It compares the result byte-for-byte with `apps/stage/src/generated/segment-commands.json`, and `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites the file. footage.rs:613 sets the precedent for a Rust test reading a stage file. `standingCommands` then reads the JSON. The stage keeps exactly one presentation rule of its own: `!vote` shows only while a poll is open. The stage stays offline-capable, because the JSON is bundled, and drift becomes a red `cargo test` instead of a wrong card on air.

## Flow
- write the golden test first (fails: file absent)
- generate the JSON with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; commit
- write onair.test.ts cases for SEG-02A !propose and the args (fail against the hand list)
- replace the CommandRow constants and switch with a lookup over the JSON, keeping the vote-while-poll rule
- DESIGN.md: replace 'copied' with 'generated + gated by cargo test'

## Expected impact
Viewers in SEG-02A learn that they can propose schemes, and every command row matches what the parser accepts. A future command, argument change or segment edit cannot reach air with a stale card, because CI fails first. This also removes the stage's last hand copy of daemon rules from OnAir.

## Evaluation
Claim: the on-air standing card equals the segment table for every segment.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no golden file or test, SEG-02A omits !propose, args differ)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: none

Routing note (critic, run challenge-2026-10-21): Critic: real but S-sized (two-line drift plus a golden test). Re-verify at HEAD: another session changed seg-02a.toml after the card was written.
evidence: apps/stage/src/OnAir.tsx:43 `const PROPOSE: CommandRow = { cmd: "!propose", args: "<scheme>", what: "Propose a scheme. Rank-gated." };` | OnAir.tsx:54-55 `case "SEG-02A": return [HINT, GRADE];` | command.rs:41-44 `name: "propose", args: "<text>", what: "Propose a scheme. Rank-gated.", rank_gated: true` | seg-02a.toml:24 `commands = ["hint", "grade", "propose", "vote"]` | grep COMMAND_SPECS: only command.rs, daemon/catalog.rs, console testgen.ts (a test fixture copy), stage OnAir.tsx comment
instrument: the card's own acceptance cases, trimmed to its S core

title: Hello and audio carry engine identity and sentence cost as fields, not prose
body:
## Summary
The sidecar announces which engine it runs by writing a sentence into `reason`, and the daemon decides whether the voice is ready by substring-matching that sentence. Per-sentence cost (render time, how long a rendered sentence waited for its turn, viseme time) exists in the sidecar and is printed to stderr, where the daemon throws it away. Make both typed: an `engine` object on hello and timing fields on audio, parsed by the daemon and shown by `voice say`.

## Description
Leans on voice-io `engine-abstraction`: 'callers branch on capability, never on identity', and absent / broken / ready must be distinguishable - today the daemon branches on a phrase, and 'warm failed to load, fell back' vs 'warm not installed' are both prose. Also voice-io `real-time-synthesis-budget`: an engine's speed is a measured figure, and the protocol is the one place it can be measured per sentence without scraping logs. Additive fields under protocol 1; reason keeps its words, so old daemons and old sidecars interoperate both ways. The daemon's hello_state branches on engine.kind and falls back to the substring only when the field is absent.

## Flow
- sidecar hello(): build engine = {kind: warm|process|none, workers?, load_ms?, fallback?} beside the unchanged reason
- Sidecar._speak: stamp render_ms (render.took_ms), held_ms (send time minus render done), face_ms (viseme time) on each audio line
- daemon SidecarLine::Hello gains engine: Option<EngineHello>; probe::hello_state(cfg, visemes, reason, engine)
- Rendered gains render_ms/held_ms/face_ms: Option<u32>; cli `voice say` prints them
- contract appendix documents the fields and retires 'The hello has no field for it'

## Expected impact
A wording change in the sidecar can no longer flip the voice to degraded; operators see where a sentence's latency went (render vs queue vs face) in `voice say` and replays, which is the input every later latency decision needs.

## Evaluation
Claim: engine identity and sentence cost are machine-readable on the wire.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no engine field, substring decides readiness, no timing fields)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (Python protocol tests, Rust on_line/hello_state tests)
Result: better
Gate: contract

Routing note (critic, run challenge-2026-10-21): Critic: an honest S (additive hello/audio fields plus a parse branch); the daemon still matches the hello's reason text.
instrument: the card's own acceptance cases, trimmed to its S core
